name: Stripe

auth.keyHelp: Click Create restricted key, set every resource to None except the ones you want read (Balance, Charges, Customers, Subscriptions, Invoices), and leave Write off.

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Stripe authenticates with HTTP Basic (key as username, empty password) and also accepts Authorization: Bearer <key> (the auth page documents both). A restricted key (rk_live_ / rk_test_) can be read-only: each resource is set to None, Read or Write, and Write implies Read, so give it Read only and the write action will fail with a permission error. There is no deeper issuing URL than the API keys page; the docs say to click Create restricted key there (live and sandbox keys are separate; the page toggles between them). The key is shown once and a live restricted key you create yourself cannot be revealed again. The docs name no specific permission for GET /v1/balance, so the Read permission on the Balance resource is assumed from the 'GET = read' rule and was not read verbatim. Stripe-Version is pinned to 2026-10-28.endive, the current version on the versioning page today; without the header requests use the account's default version. Official MCP server: https://mcp.stripe.com, OAuth, or an agent-tagged API key as a bearer token. The MCP docs say that from December 2026 the MCP server stops accepting full-access secret keys and restricted keys that are not agent-tagged. That change is stated only for the MCP server, not the REST API. Agent-tagged restricted keys are an option on key creation and are subject to Stripe approval rules for sensitive actions.
